title: We built an AI tool that grades traders. Heres the score it’ll give you:
author: Altruistic_Shoe7967
selftext:
After building a risk model and training on 4k+ wallets off Hyperliquid, we built a credit scoring / underwriting system based off it. The idea is that profitable traders can have a credit line drawn to give them exposure to leverage, without the overcollateralization of defi or the terms of prop firms designed to make you fail. Then, the trader has access to more leverage with less restriction, while a lender gets access to skilled trading strategies with lower risk. 

Feel free to DM ur wallet, and we can generate you a score and credit line, as well as the rates we’d give you on our platform.

From there, we’d love to hear what you think about our terms, ideas, and execution. Is there anything you’d add/remove from the process? Let us know what you think about our terms of if you’d use the service to trade.

comments.author: Scott_Malkinsons
comments.body:
>The idea is that profitable traders can have a credit line drawn to give them exposure to leverage, without the overcollateralization of defi or the terms of prop firms designed to make you fail.

That ain't how leverage works, Champ. If I want more leverage on self-funded accounts I can just use an off-shore brokerage, and you don't even seen to understand the difference between leverage and credit lines.

Leverage is where I might deposit $1 and you spot me so I can trade $100. If I lose $1, you margin call me, and walk away with your $99 that you put in. Credit line is where I borrow money, lose it, and then owe you a debt because I'm a moron, and you're probably a moron too because you loaned money out like that without the ability to margin call me.

Frankly, if you wanted to go this route and offer credit lines, **you'd be better off giving the credit lines to the losers so you can double dip**. They would lose the money, owe you a debt, you charge interest and penalties, plus you can mirror their trades for a profit with leverage so you multiply the double dip. "but reversing what they do won't work" ... uhh yeah, it does, because that's exactly what a trade is. The person on the other end did the opposite of what you did and made money from your loss. That's why most trades aren't even hitting the real market, it's just your broker taking the opposite side.

Why you're trying to make money **offering winners a credit line is absurd**, no no no, that's not how you do it. **You offer the losers credit, and the winners leverage**. Then you multi-dip by mirroring the losers and copying the winners.

replies.author: Beautiful_Test_1410
replies.body: ???? A credit line where someone just "owes a debt" after losing borrowed money only works if there's a way to actually collect that debt: courts, collections, a legal identity attached to the loss. There isn't one here. This is non-custodial. Nobody can sue a wallet. So the model was never going to be built on "borrow, lose, now you're in debt," that's not a mechanism DeFi even has access to.
